clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient presents with longstanding type 2 diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and CKD. Heavy proteinuria, micro‑albuminuria, and trace glucosuria point to diabetic nephropathy as the dominant driver of renal dysfunction, especially given the absence of documented antidiabetic therapy. Hypertension and ACE‑inhibitor use suggest a contributory hypertensive nephrosclerosis component. Metabolic syndrome underlies the cardiovascular risk profile, predisposing to CAD, HFpEF, PAD, and NAFLD. Anemia is explained by CKD‑related EPO deficiency, but the concurrent thrombocytosis and borderline low hematocrit raise the possibility of iron‑deficiency anemia. Discrepancies in eGFR and low urine specific gravity raise suspicion for renovascular disease. Unexplained bilirubinuria, mild ketonuria, and platelet elevation remain pending further work‑up.

Persistent bilirubinuria without documented hepatic disease
Mild ketonuria and trace glucosuria in the setting of unknown serum glucose/A1c

recommended_workup: Fasting plasma glucose and HbA1c to assess current glycaemic control
Repeat serum creatinine with CKD‑EPI eGFR calculation and spot urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio (UACR) for accurate CKD staging
Iron studies (Ferritin, transferrin saturation) and CRP to differentiate iron‑deficiency anemia from anemia of chronic disease
Renal‑artery duplex ultrasound or CTA/MRA to evaluate for atherosclerotic renal‑artery stenosis
Full‑night polysomnography or validated home sleep study to quantify OSA severity
Resting ECG, BNP, and transthoracic echocardiogram (including diastolic function) to screen for CAD and HFpEF
Liver function panel (ALT, AST, GGT, ALP, total and direct bilirubin) plus abdominal ultrasound or FibroScan for NAFLD/NASH assessment
Ankle‑brachial index (ABI) to screen for peripheral arterial disease
Thyroid function tests (TSH, free T4) to rule out hypothyroidism
Comprehensive medication reconciliation including OTC and herbal products to exclude nephrotoxic exposures
If thrombocytosis persists, JAK2 V617F PCR and peripheral blood smear to evaluate for essential thrombocythemia
